executive_summary: USD/SEK closed at 9.9901 on 2026-09-29 and EUR/SEK at 11.3325, both the highest closes of the past 52 weeks; both pairs are inverted, so a rising quote is a WEAKER krona. Over one month USD/SEK rose 4.31% and EUR/SEK 1.85%, over three months 3.23% and 2.42%, over six months 5.70% and 3.87%, and over one year 4.99% and 2.56% - the krona has lost ground to the dollar on every horizon and sits at the 100th percentile of its 52-week close range against USD, EUR, GBP and SGD. The dominant narrative is a collision between a strong domestic cycle and a hostile global one: Swedish GDP grew 1.6% q/q and 3.3% y/y in Q2, the manufacturing PMI reached 58.1 in September and the Riksbank turned hawkish on 2026-09-24, while the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00%, the US 10-year rose 45bp in a month to 5.24% and Brent held near $100. Valuation is modestly cheap: the BIS REER of 94.83 for August 2026 is about 5% below its 2020 base, at the 31st percentile of its January-2024-onward history and 2.37 points weaker in a year, and the Riksbank's own forecast assumes the KIX krona strengthens. The key tension is that the Riksbank's new path (Q4 2026 average 1.85%, Q1 2027 2.07%) and markets pricing about 125bp of hikes coexist with CPIF inflation of 0.7% and CPIF ex energy of 0.5%, so the hiking cycle rests on a forecast that measured inflation will rebound as temporary tax cuts expire, and the krona still pays 212.5bp of negative carry to the dollar. We are Bearish tactically (conviction 2, net score -0.212) because the dollar, momentum and a fragile government formation dominate four weeks, and Bullish strategically (conviction 3, net score +0.258) because the hiking path, growth outperformance against the euro area and deep undervaluation compound over one to six months. Our six-month USD/SEK target is 9.55 (EUR/SEK 10.95), below the Trading Economics consensus of 9.97 at end-Q4 and 9.75 at twelve months; the caveat is that a stronger-for-longer Fed can keep USD/SEK above 10.00 until the 2026-11-04 Riksbank decision.

tactical.analysis: The Riksbank held the policy rate at 1.75% on 2026-09-24 for the eighth consecutive meeting, decided unanimously on 2026-09-23 and effective 2026-09-30, but said the rate 'should be raised more going forward than projected in the June forecast' and that increases are expected to begin this year. At 1.75% the krona ranks 8th of the 10 rate-setters in G10+SGD, above only the BoJ (1.25%) and the SNB (0.00%): it pays 285bp to the RBA, 275bp to Norges Bank, 225bp to the Fed's 4.00% upper bound (212.5bp to the 3.875% effective rate), 200bp to the BoE, 100bp to the RBNZ, 75bp to the ECB deposit rate and 50bp to the BoC. The new path averages 1.85% in Q4 2026 and 2.07% in Q1 2027, which embeds roughly a 50% chance of a 25bp hike on 2026-11-04 and a near-certain move by December; Citi sees December as more likely. Markets are ahead of the bank: BBH estimates about 125bp of hikes priced against roughly 75bp in the path, and the 2-year SGB at 2.65% sits 90bp above the policy rate. The 10-year SGB reached 3.27% on 2026-10-01, the highest since April 2011, yet still 28bp below Bunds and 197bp below Treasuries, so the curve (about +62bp 2s10s) is steepening on term premium rather than on Swedish policy. Carry is decisively negative against the high-yielders: -212.5bp against USD on 7.50% 60-day realised vol is a carry-to-vol of -0.28, and the Eurex USD/SEK futures roll costs 248.2bp a year. Over four weeks the hawkish repricing is already in the price while the carry drag accrues every day, so the factor nets to Neutral; our own expectation for 2026-11-04 is a 45% hike probability, about 10 points below what forwards imply. The first hard test is the September CPIF flash on 2026-10-07, which feeds directly into the November decision probability.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the relevant question is the direction of differentials, and here the krona is unusually well placed: the Riksbank is one of only a handful of G10 central banks with an explicit hiking path from a low base, while the Fed (3.75-4.00% after 2026-09-16), the RBA (4.60%) and Norges Bank (4.50%) are at or near their peaks. The minutes published on 2026-09-30 show every Executive Board member moving hawkish; Seim argued the neutral rate could exceed 2.25% and, with Governor Thedéen, favoured a November hike, and only Hjelm opposed a path containing up to three increases. Danske Bank forecasts hikes in November, February and March to 2.50%, and the NIER on 2026-09-30 forecast 2.00% at end-2026 and 2.50% at end-2027. Delivered, that path narrows the krona's deficit to the ECB deposit rate from 75bp to zero, to the Fed from 225bp to about 150bp, and to Norges Bank from 275bp to about 200bp, so the forward differential trajectory turns in the krona's favour against every European peer. The constraint is that CPIF ex energy is only 0.5%, so the path rests on the Riksbank's forecast that core CPIF reaches 2.0% in 2027 as temporary fiscal measures lapse; if that rebound fails, the first hike slips into 2027. Carry remains negative throughout the horizon - the six-month cost of a long krona position against the dollar is about 1,060 pips at 212.5bp - so the bullish case is about differential momentum and valuation, not yield. We hold Bullish at 55%, a modest confidence that reflects the inflation contingency. We expect a delivered November or December hike to lift the 2-year SGB towards 2.9%, turning the front-end spread to Bunds further in the krona's favour.

tactical.analysis: Swedish data are split between very strong activity and very weak measured inflation. CPI rose only 0.3% y/y in August (-0.3% m/m), CPIF 0.7% against a 0.8% consensus, and CPIF ex energy - the Riksbank's preferred underlying measure - 0.5%, unchanged from July and below the bank's own 0.7% projection; food prices fell 6.6% y/y because of the temporary food tax cut, while transport rose 1.7% as diesel climbed 18%. Distance to the 2% CPIF target is therefore 1.3pp on the headline target measure and 1.5pp on the core, although the Riksbank estimates core inflation excluding fiscal measures is close to 2%. Growth is the opposite: GDP rose 1.6% q/q and 3.3% y/y in Q2 (revised up from 1.4%), the strongest since early 2024, on 3.5% investment growth including weapons systems and 0.9% household consumption. Leading indicators are strong - the Swedbank/Silf manufacturing PMI rose to 58.1 in September from 56.3, and the NIER economic tendency indicator rose for a fifth month with consumer confidence at its highest since December 2021 - but the July GDP indicator fell 0.8% m/m and industrial production 3.6%. The labour market lags: unemployment was 8.5% unadjusted and 8.7% seasonally adjusted in August, with 505,200 unemployed, up 19,300 in a year, although employment rose 102,600. The next tests are the September CPIF flash on 2026-10-07 and the final print with CPIF ex energy on 2026-10-14; we expect CPIF ex energy to stay at 0.5-0.7%, which would leave the hawkish narrative unvalidated for another month. Strong growth and weak inflation cancel at a four-week horizon, so the factor is Neutral.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the growth gap does the work. Swedish GDP is growing 3.3% y/y against 1.2% in the euro area and 2.1% in the US, the NIER raised its 2026 forecast to 3.0% from 2.4% on 2026-09-30, and the Riksbank's September MPR projects 2.8% for 2026 and 2.4% for 2027. Inflation should normalise mechanically: the Riksbank forecasts CPIF of about 2.3% and CPIF ex energy of about 2.0% in 2027 (best available, flagged: a Phase 6 re-read of the MPR PDF returned different annual figures; the 2.0% core figure for 2027 is corroborated by Investing.com) as the temporary food-tax cut and other fiscal measures expire, the NIER forecasts CPIF of 2.6% in 2027, and firms' pricing plans in the NIER survey remain above normal. The drivers are partly cost-push (energy, with TTF up about 132% y/y and diesel up 18%) and partly demand (retail sales +6.9% y/y, house prices up 3.9-4.8% y/y, household lending growth 3.3%), so the rebound should persist once the tax effect drops out. The labour market is the weak link - unemployment of 8.7% SA is among the highest in G10+SGD, and the NIER sees it only easing to 8.2% in 2027 - which explains why underlying wage-driven inflation is not a concern. Relative to peers, Sweden combines the fastest real growth in Europe with the lowest inflation in the set, which leaves the Riksbank room to hike for growth rather than chase inflation. We are Bullish at 56% (lowered from 58% at the Phase 6 check because the MPR inflation forecasts could not be re-confirmed), contingent on the inflation rebound appearing in the data by the December MPR. The September data due on 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-14 will still be depressed by the tax measures, so the strategic signal should only become visible from the December print onward.

tactical.analysis: The global risk backdrop is mixed on the surface but hostile for a low-liquidity, European-beta currency. The VIX was 16.39 on 2026-10-01, little changed on the month (+0.05), at the 35th percentile of its one-year range and the 46th of ten years, and the S&P 500 stood at 7,704.65 on 2026-10-01, up 14.7% y/y. Beneath that, credit widened: US high-yield spreads rose 59bp in September to 324bp, the 98th percentile of their one-year range, and investment-grade spreads reached 86bp, the 94th percentile of the year - both are widening from tight levels. The bigger shock is rates and energy - the US 10-year rose 45bp to 5.24%, the 2-year sits at 4.78%, and Brent traded $100.17 on 2026-10-01, up roughly 56% y/y, against the backdrop of the US-Iran confrontation around Hormuz. This is a transitioning regime: equities are holding, but rising real yields (10-year TIPS 2.88%) and widening high-yield spreads are the conditions in which the krona historically underperforms, because it trades as a European-growth beta with a liquidity penalty. The krona's realised behaviour confirms it: in a month when the VIX barely moved, SEK lost 4.31% to the dollar and 5.60% to the yen, and it is at the bottom of its 52-week range against every major except JPY. We have no quoted implied beta, but SEK's September underperformance against EUR (1.85%) during a 2.36% EUR/USD fall implies a dollar beta near 1.8 for USD/SEK. Tail risks in the window include an escalation in the Gulf, a disorderly bond sell-off and a European growth scare; each would hit SEK harder than EUR. The factor is Bearish at 54% (lowered at the Phase 6 check because one supporting oil print post-dates the valuation date).

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the risk regime is genuinely two-sided for the krona. The bear case is persistence: oil above $100 and an energy shock in Europe (TTF near EUR 73/MWh) feed a stagflationary drag on the euro-area industrial cycle that SEK depends on, while US real yields of 2.88% keep global financial conditions tight. The bull case is that the shock has a political resolution - US-Iran talks and a rebound in Gulf flows are the two channels that would cap Brent - and that a strong European manufacturing cycle continues: the German manufacturing PMI read 53.9 and the euro-area PMI 52.9 in September, both expansionary, and Swedish industry is at 58.1. SEK is a European-growth beta, so a goldilocks middle of the dollar smile - stable growth, stable oil, a Fed at its peak - is its best environment, and that scenario is plausible by early 2027. Credit is the swing variable: IG spreads at 86bp and HY at 324bp are both at the wide end of their one-year ranges and would compress if energy eases. We assign 25% to a sustained risk-off, 30% to a goldilocks recovery and 45% to a choppy middle, which nets to Neutral. Confidence is held at 50% because the factor's sign depends on an exogenous geopolitical outcome. A sustained fall in Brent below $90 would be the clearest signal that the goldilocks branch is taking over.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the same positioning becomes a two-sided signal. A krona at the 100th percentile of its range against USD, EUR and GBP, with no CFTC footprint to confirm crowding, is the kind of setup that has historically reversed when the Riksbank delivered a hike - the 2023 hedging programme showed how a single official flow can move EUR/SEK several percent. Without a measured positioning series we cannot claim an extreme, so the factor is Neutral at 45%, with a contrarian bullish tilt that we do not score. Hedging by Swedish banks and corporates is not observable in public data, which is a further reason to keep the score at Neutral. A first Riksbank hike is the natural catalyst for exporters to raise hedge ratios on foreign-currency receipts, a flow that has historically supported the krona. The risk is that the 'SEK puzzle' persists - structural outflows from pension savers and a liquidity discount have kept the krona cheap through previous hiking cycles. A squeeze in EUR/SEK from 11.33 to the 10.85-10.96 support zone (about 3.5%) is plausible after the first hike; positioning is therefore a mildly bullish signal at strategic horizons, which we leave unscored because it cannot be measured.

tactical.analysis: Sweden's external position is strong in stock terms but deteriorating at the margin. The current account surplus was SEK 126.2bn in Q2 2026, the largest since Q1 2025 and 6.45% of GDP on the OECD vintage, but its composition has shifted: primary income contributed SEK 100.9bn as investment returns rose, while the goods surplus narrowed to SEK 67.7bn from 86.5bn a year earlier. The monthly trade data then turned: August posted a SEK 11.9bn deficit, the largest since August 2022, as imports rose 12% y/y to SEK 171.8bn and exports 10.5% to 159.9bn, with export value the lowest in a year (seasonally adjusted, still a SEK 1.7bn surplus). Terms of trade are moving against the krona: Sweden is a net energy importer outside electricity, and TTF gas near EUR 73/MWh (+132% y/y) and Brent near $100 (+56% y/y) raise the import bill, while copper at $6.49/lb is down 1.29% on the month despite being up 29% y/y. Germany remains the largest single trading partner and euro-area demand is holding (exports to the EU +15% y/y), which cushions volumes but not prices. With the next trade print due late October and energy prices still rising on the month, the near-term flow signal from the external accounts is mildly negative. We are Bearish at 51% (lowered at the Phase 6 check: the copper print post-dates the valuation date), a low-confidence call because the stock position remains a structural support. The September trade print in late October is the next data point; a second deficit would extend the bearish read.

In the krona's favour: a current account surplus of about 6.5% of GDP, a positive and growing net investment income (primary income +SEK 100.9bn in Q2), a low-carbon electricity system that shields households and industry from the worst of the European energy shock, and a real effective exchange rate of 94.83 that is about 5% below its 2020 base and 2.37 points weaker than a year ago, which supports export competitiveness. tactical.analysis: The Riksbank's communication shifted decisively hawkish in September. The decision statement of 2026-09-24 said the policy rate 'should be raised more going forward than projected in the June forecast' and that increases are expected to begin this year, the path was lifted to an average of 1.85% in Q4 2026 and 2.07% in Q1 2027, and the Q4 2027 point rose to 2.42% from 2.07%. The minutes published on 2026-09-30 reinforced the shift: Danske Bank's read is that every member moved in a more hawkish direction, that Governor Thedéen and Anna Seim explicitly favour a November hike, and that only Hjelm opposed a path with up to three increases. Deputy Governor Per Jansson put the krona at the centre of the case, noting it had depreciated by around 2% against the euro and slightly more than 4% against the dollar since the August decision - the Riksbank is unusually willing to cite the exchange rate, and SEK weakness is now a reason to hike rather than a side effect. The bank is among the most transparent in the world, publishing a rate path and attributed minutes, and its track record of following its path in 2024-25 supports credibility; markets already price more tightening (about 125bp) than the path itself (about 75bp), the opposite of a credibility gap. Seim's caution that 'the policy rate path is a forecast, not a promise' is the one dovish note. The next communication events are the September CPIF data, speeches in October and the Monetary Policy Update on 2026-11-04. We are Bullish at 60%: guidance is the clearest krona-positive signal available over four weeks.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months credibility is the krona's structural asset. The Riksbank has published a path that rises to about 2.4% by end-2027, the NIER independently forecasts 2.50% at end-2027 and 2.75% in early 2028, and Danske Bank expects three hikes by March 2027, so domestic forecasters, the bank and markets are aligned on direction. The bank's reaction function now explicitly includes the exchange rate as an inflation risk, and its September MPR assumes the KIX krona strengthens over the forecast - a forecast that also lowers the bank's own inflation projection, so if the krona does not appreciate the bank has a reason to hike more. Board dynamics are favourable: the most hawkish member (Seim) argues the neutral rate may exceed 2.25%, above the bank's 1.5-3% range midpoint, and only one member dissents from the path. The risks are the 0.5% CPIF ex energy print and the bank's admission that spare capacity remains; if the December MPR has to lower the path, guidance would turn into a credibility cost. The new government (centre-left, 176 seats) has not signalled any challenge to Riksbank independence. We hold Bullish at 58%, slightly below tactical because six months gives more time for inflation data to undercut the path. The December MPR on 2026-12-16 is therefore the key credibility test inside the horizon.

tactical.analysis: The near-term event calendar carries more domestic political risk than usual. The general election of 2026-09-13 gave the centre-left bloc (S, V, MP, C) 176 of 349 seats and 49.5% of the vote against 173 seats and 48.8% for the right bloc, a one-seat working majority built from four parties with differing coalition preferences; the Social Democrats posted their weakest result in more than a century and the Sweden Democrats fell for the first time since entering parliament. Speaker Andreas Norlén has tasked Magdalena Andersson with forming a government, and the Riksdag opened on 2026-09-28, but no prime-ministerial vote date had been fixed by 2026-10-01; an election-year budget will follow the new government rather than precede it. Fiscal direction is the market variable: the outgoing government left SEK 50bn of reform room for 2027-2030 while the NIER estimates about SEK 120bn, and a centre-left coalition is likely to use more of it. Externally, the US-Iran confrontation around Hormuz keeps Brent near $100 and is the main tail risk for a European energy importer, and a fresh escalation would hit a low-liquidity currency first. The three dated events with the largest FX impact inside four weeks are the CPIF releases on 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-14, the FOMC and the RBNZ/BoC on 2026-10-28, and the expected prime-ministerial vote (2026-10-W3, not yet scheduled). Tail scenarios: a failed first PM vote and prolonged formation (20%, EUR/SEK +1.5%), a Gulf escalation pushing Brent above $115 (15%, EUR/SEK +2-3%), and a US-Iran agreement (10%, EUR/SEK -2%). Event-vol premia cannot be measured because SEK has no listed options. The factor is Bearish at a low 52%.

A centre-left government is likely to be more expansionary than the outgoing Tidö coalition, but the NIER's SEK 120bn estimate of budget room shows the expansion can be financed without breaching the framework, and modest fiscal stimulus in a 3%-growth economy reinforces the Riksbank's hiking case rather than undermining the currency. The external geopolitical tail - the Gulf and European energy security - remains the dominant risk, but it is symmetric over six months: escalation hurts, a deal helps, and both are plausible. Swedish banks' Baltic exposure and the housing market are background risks with no current trigger: house prices are rising 3.9-4.8% y/y and household lending is growing 3.3%. The factor is Neutral at 50%. The incoming government's first budget, expected in the second half of November, will set the fiscal impulse for 2027. A smooth formation would let the political premium in the krona erode over the first quarter.

tactical.analysis: Sweden's fiscal position remains among the strongest in G10 even as deficits widen. Riksgälden's May forecast (published 2026-05-28, older than the 60-day strategic window; latest published, flagged) puts the central government deficit at SEK 196bn in 2026 and 208bn in 2027, driven by defence spending, tax cuts and energy-relief measures, with central government debt rising from 21% to 23% of GDP; the outgoing finance minister projected a general government financial balance of -2.5% of GDP in 2026 and -2.0% in 2027, with a structural balance of -1.5%. Issuance is rising: nominal bond supply goes to SEK 220bn in 2026 and 240bn in 2027, with weekly SEK 5bn auctions since 17 June, and 10-year SGB yields at 3.27% on 2026-10-01 are the highest since April 2011 - higher supply is part of the term premium. S&P affirmed AAA with a stable outlook on 2026-06-05; Moody's (Aaa) and Fitch (AAA) carry the top rating per the currency brief, with no 2026 action by either retrieved, and no rating action is scheduled in the window. Sovereign CDS has no free quote, but nothing in pricing suggests credit concern. Interest costs are low because debt is low, and fiscal space is ample: even the NIER's larger SEK 120bn reform-room estimate keeps debt below 30% of GDP. Over four weeks the factor is a background strength with no catalyst, so it is Neutral at 60%. No rating review is scheduled before the 2026-11-04 Riksbank decision.

strategic.analysis: Over six months fiscal policy is more likely to support the krona at the margin than to hurt it. A centre-left government will present the 2027 budget after it takes office, and while it is likely to spend more than the SEK 50bn reform room left by the outgoing coalition, the fiscal framework's surplus target and debt anchor bind any government, and debt of 21-23% of GDP is about a third of the euro-area average. In relative terms Sweden's AAA balance sheet is a rare asset among G10 issuers at a time of large deficits elsewhere, which makes SGBs a natural destination for reserve and real-money duration as yields reach 3.27%. Higher issuance and a modest fiscal impulse also lift neutral real rates, supporting the Riksbank's path. The risk is a budget that materially overshoots the framework, which we see as unlikely (10%). We keep the factor Neutral at 58% (lowered at the Phase 6 check because the Debt Office forecast is stale) because no fiscal catalyst is strong enough to move the currency on its own. Even a fiscal impulse of 1% of GDP would leave central government debt in the mid-20s as a share of GDP in 2027 on Riksgalden's baseline. The relevant risk is not solvency but term premium, which already shows up in the 10-year yield.

tactical.rationale: At tactical weights the result is decided by USD Liquidity (0.11), Risk Appetite (0.10) and Flows (0.10), which together contribute -0.168, against a single meaningful krona-positive block, Guidance (+0.042). Policy and Rates (0.24) and Inflation and Growth (0.18) carry the largest weights but score zero: the hawkish Riksbank path is already priced at the short end (about 125bp of hikes against roughly 75bp in the path), and very strong growth (GDP +3.3% y/y, PMI 58.1) is offset by CPIF ex energy of 0.5%. The net score of -0.212 therefore sits in the Bearish band (-0.10 to -0.30) and maps to conviction 2. The factor interactions are the core of the call: the krona-negative forces - a Fed at 3.75-4.00%, a US 10-year at 5.24%, widening high-yield spreads, Brent near $100 and an unresolved government formation - are global and fast-moving, while the krona-positive forces - guidance, growth, valuation - are domestic and need data to validate them, and the next CPIF prints (2026-10-07 flash, 2026-10-14 final) are still depressed by temporary tax cuts. What is priced is a hawkish Riksbank; what is not priced is a further month of dollar strength, which we expect to carry USD/SEK into the 10.00-10.15 resistance band (round number plus the 200-week average at 10.1523). The path of least resistance is a grind higher in USD/SEK with EUR/SEK broadly stable at 11.30-11.45, because the euro shares the dollar headwind. The key dates are 2026-10-14 (Swedish and US CPI), 2026-10-28 (FOMC) and 2026-11-04 (Riksbank MPU), and the expected prime-ministerial vote around 2026-10-W3. Conviction is held at 2 rather than 3 because positioning is unmeasurable (no CFTC, no options) and the krona already sits at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range against USD, EUR and GBP, which makes a sharp squeeze possible on any hawkish surprise. Actionability is moderate: a short-krona position against USD earns 212.5bp of carry, so the cost of being early is low, but the expected move to 10.12 (1.3%) is small against a 14-day ATR of 876 pips, and we would not hold it through the 2026-11-04 decision. Our expected one-month level of 10.12 sits about 1,500 pips above the derived forward. A hawkish surprise in the Swedish CPI data on 2026-10-14 is the main risk to the call.

strategic.rationale: At strategic weights Policy and Rates (0.24), External Balance (0.16), Guidance (0.12) and USD Liquidity (0.12) dominate. Policy and Rates contributes +0.132 because the Riksbank is one of very few G10 central banks with an explicit hiking path from a low base while the Fed, RBA and Norges Bank are at or near their peaks; Guidance adds +0.070 because the September minutes show the whole board moving hawkish and the bank citing krona weakness as a reason to act; and Inflation and Growth adds +0.056 because GDP growth of 3.3% y/y against 1.2% in the euro area and the expiry of temporary tax cuts should lift CPIF towards 2.3% in 2027 (Riksbank MPR; best available, flagged). External Balance, USD Liquidity, Risk, Flows, Event Risk, Fiscal and Market Structure all score Neutral: each has offsetting forces over six months. The net score of +0.258 is Bullish and maps to conviction 3. The interactions reinforce: delivered hikes narrow the krona's deficits to the ECB (75bp to about zero) and the Fed (225bp to about 150bp) while the Fed's balance sheet is no longer shrinking and its hiking cycle approaches its end, and a REER of 94.83 leaves room for appreciation without a valuation headwind. The conflict is inflation: CPIF ex energy at 0.5% means the path is a forecast that must be validated by the December MPR. What is priced is a hiking cycle at the front end; what is not priced is its pass-through into the spot rate, so forwards (USD/SEK 9.8665 at six months) sit well above our 9.55 target. The path of least resistance is a U-shape: weakness into late October, a turn around 2026-11-04, and a grind lower in EUR/SEK towards 10.95 and USD/SEK towards 9.55 by end-Q1 2027. Key dates are 2026-11-04, 2026-12-16 (MPR), 2027-02-03 and 2027-03-24. Conviction drivers are the alignment of Riksbank, NIER and Danske forecasts on 2.50% by 2027 and the krona's extreme range position; actionability is best in EUR/SEK, where the carry cost is only 75bp a year. The main risk to the call is a December path cut, which we assign a 25% probability.

consensus_divergence.consensus_view: Consensus is krona-positive but slow. The Trading Economics model path has USD/SEK at 9.97 at end-Q4 2026 and 9.75 in twelve months, and EUR/SEK at 11.268 and 11.165; ING's last published year-end EUR/SEK target was 10.60 (May 2026). On rates, the Riksbank path implies about 75bp of tightening over twelve months, the NIER forecasts 2.00% at end-2026 and 2.50% at end-2027, Danske Bank expects 2.50% by March 2027, and markets price about 125bp.
consensus_divergence.our_view: We are more krona-bearish than consensus for the next four weeks (USD/SEK 10.12 against a consensus that sees the pair already peaking near 10.0) and more krona-bullish over six months: USD/SEK 9.55 and EUR/SEK 10.95 by end-Q1 2027, against an interpolated consensus near 9.90 and 11.23. On rates we expect slightly less tightening than markets price (50-75bp by mid-2027).
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: About 1,500 pips more krona-bearish at one month (10.12 vs about 9.97); about 3,500 pips more krona-bullish at six months (9.55 vs about 9.90); in EUR/SEK about 2,800 pips (10.95 vs about 11.23). Against the forward curve the six-month edge is about 3,165 pips.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Tactically, consensus models anchor to rate differentials and undervaluation and under-weight the dollar's momentum and the krona's liquidity penalty in a risk shock: in September SEK lost 4.31% to the dollar while the VIX barely moved. Strategically, consensus extrapolates the 'SEK puzzle' - a currency that fails to respond to its fundamentals - and therefore projects only gradual appreciation. We think the combination of a delivered hiking cycle, a Fed balance sheet that is no longer shrinking and a REER about 5% below its 2020 base is a regime the puzzle does not cover: the Riksbank is now explicitly targeting krona weakness as an inflation risk, which changes the reaction function. We also think the market over-prices the size of the hiking cycle and under-prices its transmission to spot, which is why we differ on rates and on FX in opposite directions.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: A long-krona position from 9.99 to 9.55 earns about 4.4% in spot against a six-month forward of 9.8665, an edge of about 3,165 pips; in EUR/SEK, 10.95 against a six-month forward near 11.30 (from the -65.9bp Eurex roll) is an edge of about 3.1%.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If consensus is right on speed, a long-krona position earns little spot and pays 212.5bp of carry against USD; in EUR/SEK the cost is only 75bp. The genuine loss case is a December MPR that cuts the path with the Fed still firm, taking USD/SEK to 10.35.

forward_vs_spot.interpretation: Forward points are DERIVED, not quoted: no free USD/SEK forward-point source exists, so outrights are built from the cached Eurex futures roll premium of -248.2bp annualised (observed 2026-09-29) at 30, 91 and 182 days on an actual/365 basis. The premium is 36bp wider than the 212.5bp effective-rate differential, the residual being basis and term. At one month our expected spot is above the forward (krona-bearish); at three and six months it is below, which is where the strategic edge lies.

key_catalysts.rationale: Services PMI was 55.8 in August. A print near or above that level, alongside the 58.1 manufacturing PMI, keeps the growth case for a November hike intact; a drop below 52 would undercut it.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - strong activity is priced into the 2y SGB at 2.65%

key_catalysts.rationale: The first read on whether measured inflation is turning up from CPIF 0.7%. A CPIF at or above 1.0% would make a November hike the base case; at or below 0.6% it would push the first hike to December.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the path embeds about 50% for November

key_catalysts.event: Sweden GDP indicator (August) and industrial production
key_catalysts.rationale: July GDP fell 0.8% m/m and industrial production 3.6%; a rebound would confirm Q2's 1.6% q/q as the trend, a second fall would challenge the Riksbank's 2.8% growth forecast.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - monthly GDP is noisy and rarely moves the krona unless it confirms a trend

key_catalysts.event: Sweden CPI final including CPIF ex energy (September); US CPI (September)
key_catalysts.rationale: CPIF ex energy, the Riksbank's preferred underlying gauge, was 0.5% in August; we expect 0.5-0.7%. The same day's US CPI (August headline 3.4%, core 2.4%) sets the tone for the FOMC.
Unemployment was 8.7% seasonally adjusted in August; the Riksbank forecasts 8.6% for 2026. A stable print changes little; a rise above 9% would revive the dovish minority view.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully - spare capacity is acknowledged by the Riksbank

key_catalysts.event: Riksdag prime-ministerial vote (expected; date not confirmed as of 2026-10-01)
key_catalysts.rationale: A successful vote for Magdalena Andersson on a 176-seat bloc removes the main domestic tail risk; a failed first vote would extend uncertainty and weigh on the krona for one to two weeks.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - formation risk is in the krona's discount

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision (also Bank of Canada and RBNZ)
key_catalysts.rationale: The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16; a firm hold with hawkish guidance keeps the dollar bid and USD/SEK near 10.10, while a clear signal that the cycle is over would mark the krona's tactical low.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - one more hike is partly priced

key_catalysts.rationale: A hold at 2.50% is expected. A hawkish ECB would keep EUR/SEK supported and reduce the krona's relative-rates advantage; a clear pause would make EUR/SEK the cleanest krona-bullish expression.
A further BoJ hike would extend the SEK/JPY fall (already -5.6% over one month) but has little effect on the krona elsewhere.

key_catalysts.event: MAS semi-annual monetary policy review (expected late October; not in the authoritative meetings file)
key_catalysts.rationale: Consensus expects a further steepening of the S$NEER slope; a tightening would extend SGD/SEK strength (already at the 100th percentile of its range) without changing the krona's direction elsewhere.
The RBA hiked to 4.60% on 2026-09-29; a hold is expected. The decision matters for AUD/SEK, the krona's worst G10 cross on the year (+13.23%), not for its direction.

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank decision and Monetary Policy Update
key_catalysts.rationale: The pivotal event for both horizons. A 25bp hike to 2.00% (our probability 45%) or an explicit December signal would mark the inflection from tactical krona weakness to strategic strength; a dovish hold with a lower path would invalidate the strategic view.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - about 50% priced in the path; markets price about 125bp over 12-24 months

key_catalysts.event: Bank of England (Monetary Policy Report) and Norges Bank decisions
key_catalysts.rationale: Markets price close to 80% for a BoE hike; Norges Bank is expected to hold at 4.50%. Both matter for the crosses, not for the krona's direction.

key_catalysts.event: 2027 budget bill from the incoming government (election-year timetable; date not confirmed)
key_catalysts.rationale: A centre-left budget is likely to use more than the outgoing government's SEK 50bn reform room; a moderate impulse within the framework supports the Riksbank's path, an overshoot would raise term premium.

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: New dots will show whether the Fed sees 3.75-4.00% as the peak; a lower terminal path would support the strategic krona view.

key_catalysts.event: Riksbank decision and Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The December MPR is where the path is either validated by data or cut. Our base case is a hike by this meeting and a path that keeps 2.25-2.50% for 2027.
Danske Bank expects the second hike here; by this date the temporary tax effects should be visibly fading from CPIF.
The third hike in the Danske Bank profile, to 2.50%; the end-point of our six-month horizon.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced at the spot level

invalidators.condition: CPIF ex energy prints at or below 0.4% y/y on 2026-10-14 or 2026-11-13
invalidators.mechanism: A falling underlying rate would make the Riksbank's 2.0% core forecast for 2027 implausible and push the first hike into 2027, removing the strategic case.

invalidators.condition: The Riksbank holds on 2026-11-04 AND lowers the Q1 2027 path point below 1.95%
invalidators.mechanism: A lower path would reverse the guidance factor and the policy factor at once; EUR/SEK would retest 11.45-11.55.

invalidators.condition: USD/SEK closes above 10.25 for five consecutive sessions
invalidators.mechanism: A sustained break of the 200-week average and the 10.16-10.25 zone would signal a regime change in the dollar rather than a cyclical move, invalidating the strategic Bullish call.

invalidators.condition: EUR/SEK closes below 11.13 for five sessions before 2026-10-28
invalidators.mechanism: A krona rally against the euro before the dollar turns would show the hawkish repricing transmitting faster than we assume, removing the tactical Bearish call.

invalidators.condition: Brent rises above $115 for two weeks
invalidators.mechanism: A deeper energy shock widens the trade deficit, hits European growth and keeps the dollar bid, overriding the Riksbank's hawkishness at both horizons.

invalidators.condition: The US 10-year Treasury yield falls below 4.75% before 2026-10-28
invalidators.mechanism: A reversal of the September US rates shock would release the main tactical pressure on the krona and move USD Liquidity and Risk factors to Neutral.

invalidators.condition: A first prime-ministerial vote fails and formation runs past 2026-11-15
invalidators.mechanism: Prolonged political uncertainty would delay the budget and add a political risk premium to a low-liquidity currency, extending tactical weakness into the strategic window.

The krona moved to the 100th percentile of its 52-week range against USD, EUR and GBP; momentum is now unambiguous.
The Q2 current account surplus of SEK 126.2bn (6.45% of GDP) offsets the August trade deficit and the energy drag over six months.
The election delivered a narrow but clear bloc majority (176-173); the residual risk is formation, which resolves inside the horizon.
Higher SGB supply and a likely looser centre-left budget remove the tactical fiscal premium; the AAA position is a background constant.

seasonality.pattern: Year-end liquidity. The framework documents year-end portfolio rebalancing as a pattern for all currencies, and the currency brief documents that the krona is among the least liquid G10 currencies with spreads that widen outside core hours. Thin December liquidity combined with year-end dollar funding demand has historically left the krona vulnerable to outsized moves in the second half of December.
seasonality.relevance_window: 2026-12-15 to 2027-01-05, inside the strategic horizon and just after the 2026-12-16 Riksbank MPR.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: Not quantified from a verified source this cycle; treated as a volatility risk rather than a directional signal.
seasonality.current_alignment: Neutral to slightly krona-negative: the year-end window coincides with the December MPR, so a hawkish MPR could be partly offset by seasonal dollar demand.

assumptions: Policy rates are the latest decision actuals in Data-Cache/calendar/events (SEK 1.75 verified against the 2026-09-24 row); EUR is the ECB deposit facility rate (2.50%; MRO 2.65%) and USD is the target-range upper bound (4.00%) in the rate table and the 3.875% effective midpoint for carry. CBPOL_AU and CBPOL_NO are stale and were overridden; policy legs in derived/*.json were not used.

Price analytics (spot, moving averages, realised vol, ATR, 52-week ranges, zones) were re-derived with Automation/Scripts/derive.py on the gated store truncated to the 2026-09-29 close - the common anchor of this cycle - because the live derived files had rolled forward to 2026-10-02, after the valuation date.

Carry-to-vol ratios are annualised policy carry divided by 60-day realised volatility from the re-derived analytics; no implied vol exists for any SEK pair, and no cross volatility was built from two USD legs. NZD/SEK has no file in the store and is a documented gap.

Forward points are derived from the cached Eurex futures roll premium (USD/SEK -248.2bp annualised, observed 2026-09-29), not quoted; the premium equals the rate differential plus cross-currency basis.
The PPP table is a REER-relative proxy (SEK REER 94.83 divided by each peer's BIS REER, August 2026), not an absolute PPP model; NZD/SEK has no spot in the store.
CFTC fields are placeholders because SEK is not a reportable CFTC market; positioning is read from price-store percentiles and structural flows.

Macro table: GDP, unemployment and current account are point-in-time vintages as of 2026-10-01 (cache); CPI is the most recent published print per country with its period labelled. SEK core is CPIF ex energy 0.5% (Aug 2026), verified against the event store and SCB via Trading Economics; NZD core is the RBNZ sectoral factor model 2.7% (Q2 2026); Japan CPI is research-sourced because the cache has none; SGD is research-sourced (not an OECD member).
The cached Brent series is corrupt (113.96 on 2026-09-29 against WTI 96.16) and is not quoted; Brent figures are cited web prints.

Riksbank path figures come partly from secondary reports of the September MPR (Investing.com, BBH via FXStreet, DailySweden), which differ in detail; the MPR PDF values marked 'about' are as extracted. Market pricing of about 125bp is BBH's estimate; no SEK OIS curve was available, so the 2-year SGB serves as the proxy.
Prime-ministerial vote and 2027 budget dates were not confirmed as of 2026-10-01 and are given in week format.
